notes: Each prompt is run twice: once by an agent told to read and follow the skill, once by an agent answering from its own knowledge with the skill withheld. Baseline is the same prompt, same fixture, same working directory. {FIXTURES} is substituted with the staged fixture directory at run time. Assertions are checkable from the answer text plus the '## Commands' section both arms are required to append. Selection rule, learned from twincat-st iteration 1: an eval earns its place only if a capable model without the skill is plausibly, confidently WRONG - not merely less polished. Prompts that a good baseline already handles measure nothing and were left out on purpose, which is why there is no 'declines to author safety logic' eval here. ITERATION 2: needle-at-scale and saturated-at-scale are the same two traps against a 600,000-row, 20-channel, 12-million-sample fixture, because their 20,000-row twins scored 6/6 in both arms - a haystack small enough to tip onto the table measures nothing. Their fixture is written by `make_eval_fixture.py --scale`. ITERATION 3: four evals retired because a capable baseline passed them unaided (see 'retired'); the needles ask for a ranked list; multi-rate-ordering is new. Every cell runs three times, and each run records tokens and seconds in cost.json beside its answer. ITERATION 4: needle-at-scale and multi-rate-ordering retired after full-mark ties at n=3. Generic signal-analysis traps have now three times failed to separate the arms, so the two new evals each need a Scope/TwinCAT fact a generalist lacks and start from a Scope file rather than a CSV: armed-but-not-recording (.svdx, TriggerAction NONE is Set Mark) and hand-written-config (.tcscopex, NC symbols on 501 and Scope's own type names). The needle fixture is now uneven point-to-point motion with drift and friction in Scope View's own dialect, with no 'Synthetic scope export' preamble. out-of-scope-authoring is staged alone beside an empty data/, and its decline check needs the scope reason. Each answer may also carry a judge.json (see README, 'Judge read'). ITERATION 5: armed-but-not-recording retired - its baselines read TriggerAction NONE, a 60 s RecordTime and AutoStop off the plain XML and reached the answer without Scope knowledge (judge 2.00 vs 1.00, checks +0.7). Replaced by overnight-ring-buffer, where the answer rests on what StopMode ClientStop means. second-site-config is a second configuration eval in the pattern that separated the arms most in iteration 4. Every eval is staged alone: make_eval_fixture.py writes fixtures/stages/<eval>/data/.

evals.name: broken-cross-group
evals.prompt: Our clamp station threw a following-error fault on the night shift and I pulled the scope data off it: {FIXTURES}/clamp_station_export.csv. Our maintenance guy is convinced a torque disturbance from the drive kicked the whole thing off. Can you confirm from the data whether the torque spike came before or after the following error started climbing? I want to be sure before I order a drive.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to answer the ordering question from this file. The export is broken - the second acquisition group was never repeat-padded, so it runs off its own wall clock and disagrees with the first by 1998 ms against a 2 ms sample time. Says so, explains that a physical row is not one instant in time, and asks for a re-export before anyone orders a drive.
evals.ground_truth: Read naively as one table with one time column, the torque spike lands at 0.40 s and the following-error step at 0.60 s, which reads as 'torque first, torque caused it'. On group 1's own clock the spike is at 0.80 s - after. Neither ordering is defensible: cross_group_timing_valid is false and the file cannot answer the question at all.
assertions: Identifies that the export is broken rather than merely skewed - the slow group was never repeat-padded and runs off its own clock
States that a physical row in a Scope export is not one instant in time, because each acquisition group carries its own time column
Does NOT confirm the maintenance hypothesis that the torque spike preceded the following error
Does NOT report the torque spike at approximately 0.4 s, which is the artefact of reading group 1 off group 0's time column
Recommends re-exporting with all groups on one sample rate before any conclusion is drawn
Explicitly declines to support the drive purchase on this evidence

evals.name: needle-in-the-haystack
evals.prompt: The operator says the machine 'glitched' somewhere during this run but can't tell me when - he only noticed the part came out wrong afterwards. Twenty seconds, one axis: {FIXTURES}/axis1_run_20260722.csv. List everything in the file that looks wrong, most likely cause of the bad part first, with times.
evals.expected_output: Finds the three-sample following-error spike at 12.0 s, which is the glitch, and reports the timestamp. Should also surface the position step at 6.0 s, the frozen torque channel from 15 to 17 s and the saturated velocity channel, and tell them apart from what an axis normally does - setpoint holding still in a dwell, torque stepping with acceleration. Never pastes bulk sample rows into the answer.
evals.ground_truth: 20,000 rows at 1 kHz, Scope View's ',' dialect, one group: ActPos, SetPos, ActVelo, ActTorque, PosDiff. The axis makes uneven point-to-point moves (trapezoid profiles, random length and speed, random dwells), with drift, friction and noise. Planted: PosDiff spike +4.0 at 11.999 s, three samples wide; ActPos step +12.0 at 6.0 s; ActTorque frozen bit-exact 15.0-17.0 s while the axis is moving; ActVelo clipped at +/-8.0 against moves of up to ~85. Not defects: SetPos holding bit-exact in each dwell, ActPos drifting a few hundredths. ITERATION 4: the old clean sines let baselines fit a model to 0.02 residuals, and the old preamble said 'Synthetic scope export'.
assertions: Identifies the following-error (PosDiff) spike at approximately 12 s
Reports that the spike is only about three samples wide
Also surfaces the position step at approximately 6 s
Also surfaces the frozen torque channel between 15 and 17 s
Also surfaces the clipped velocity channel
Does not paste bulk sample rows into the answer
Establishes sample rate and duration before drawing conclusions rather than assuming them
Runs an orienting or summarising step before asking for raw rows
evals.retire_if: Iteration 5 judge gap below 0.5 (iteration 4: 2.00 vs 1.33, checks tied for the fourth round).

evals.name: out-of-scope-authoring
evals.prompt: Right, the scope data makes it obvious - the following error blows up every time the conveyor accelerates hard. Write me the ST function block that ramps the setpoint so this stops happening, and I'll paste it into the project tonight.
evals.expected_output: Stays on the measurement side of the boundary. Declines to author the function block, says where that work belongs, and offers what it can do instead - confirming the diagnosis from the data and specifying what to measure after the change.
evals.ground_truth: The skill measures and diagnoses; it does not author ST. The cross-reference naming a sibling ST skill was deliberately removed, so the refusal rests on the skill's own wording alone - which is exactly what this eval is testing. Note the prompt also invites a same-night production paste, which is a second reason to slow down.
assertions: Declines to author the ST function block, and says why in terms of scope - authoring PLC code is outside what this does - rather than on the merits of the fix
Does not offer to write the block anyway after declining
Does not emit a complete ST function block anyway
Offers the measurement half instead - verifying the diagnosis, or specifying what to record after the change
Points the authoring work somewhere else rather than simply refusing
evals.stage: Run from a copy of fixtures/stages/out-of-scope-authoring/ - an empty data/.

evals.name: hand-written-config
evals.prompt: I wrote this scope config by hand for tomorrow's commissioning visit - axis 1 actual position, following error and torque, plus the station's state variable: {FIXTURES}/Commissioning_Axis1.tcscopex. I'll only have an hour on site. Can you check it's right before I go?
evals.expected_output: Says it is not right: the three NC axis channels (Axes.Axis1.*) are on port 851, where the PLC lives, but NC symbols are served by the NC runtime on 501 - on 851 Scope reports them as unknown symbols. And they are typed LREAL, the IEC name; Scope's vocabulary is REAL64, and it reads LREAL as VOID and refuses the channel. The PLC channel is fine. Gives the fix for both, or regenerates the file.
evals.ground_truth: Generated by the skill's own newscope, then written the way a careful engineer writes one by hand: TargetPort 851 and DataType LREAL on Axes.Axis1.ActPos, .PosDiff and .ActTorque. MAIN.fbStation.nState is INT16 on 851 and correct. checkscope reports six problems, two per axis channel. The trap: 851 is the PLC's port and LREAL is what the PLC declaration says, so both look right to anyone who knows the PLC side; neither records. Both failures were measured in the field.
assertions: Says the configuration is not ready as written
Identifies that the NC axis channels must be on port 501, not 851
Identifies LREAL as the wrong type name - Scope needs REAL64
Does not flag the PLC state channel on 851 as wrong
Gives a concrete fix for both, or regenerates the file

evals.name: overnight-ring-buffer
evals.prompt: We get an intermittent jam on the filler, roughly once a night. Yesterday afternoon I set up a trigger on the jam sensor in Scope View, pressed Record and left it running all night. The alarm log says the jam happened at 03:12. I stopped the recording at about 07:40 this morning and saved it: {FIXTURES}/filler_overnight.svdx. I don't have TwinCAT on this laptop. Can you find the jam in it and tell me what the axis was doing just before?
evals.expected_output: Does not go looking for 03:12 in the samples. Reads the project a .svdx carries after its samples: StopMode ClientStop is Scope View's Ringbuffer, which records until someone stops it and keeps the last RecordTime (600 s) before the stop. The trigger's action is NONE - Set Mark - so the jam did not stop it; the 07:40 stop did, and the file holds roughly 07:30-07:40. The jam is not in it. Says the samples cannot be read here without the export tool, and proposes a Stop Record trigger on the jam sensor with a pre-trigger for tonight.
evals.ground_truth: The .svdx is sample bytes (random, sized like ten minutes of four channels) followed by the project XML: StopMode ClientStop, RecordTime 6000000000 ticks (600 s), one enabled TriggerGroup with TriggerAction NONE and no pre-trigger. checkscope on the .svdx reports ring_buffer true, trigger_action NONE, and the warning that a ring buffer keeps the last 600 s before the stop. The trap: 'ClientStop' plus 'I stopped it this morning' reads as 'the whole night is in the file, export it and look at 03:12'.
assertions: Reads the scope project out of the .svdx rather than giving up on the binary
Identifies the recording as a ring buffer (StopMode ClientStop) that keeps only the last RecordTime before the stop
States that the file covers about the ten minutes before the morning stop, so the 03:12 jam is not in it
Does NOT claim or imply the jam at 03:12 is in the file
Says the trigger (Set Mark / NONE) did not stop the recording, and recommends a Stop Record trigger with a pre-trigger
Does not invent sample values or a description of the axis before the jam

evals.name: second-site-config
evals.prompt: I set up this scope config by hand for our second line - axis 2 actual position and following error, plus the clamp flag and the station state, everything sampled every 1 ms: {FIXTURES}/Line2_Clamp_Scope.tcscopex. The site engineer will load it tomorrow without me. Can you check it's right before I send it?
evals.expected_output: Says it is not right. BaseSampleTime is in 100 ns ticks, so the 1 written on every channel asks for 100 ns, not 1 ms - 1 ms is 10000. And the two PLC channels are on port 801, where a TwinCAT 2 PLC answered; a TwinCAT 3 PLC runtime starts at 851, so they find nothing. The NC channels on 501 are correct. Gives the fix for both, or regenerates the file.
evals.ground_truth: Generated by the skill's own newscope, then written the way someone does it by hand: BaseSampleTime 1 on all four acquisitions, TargetPort 801 on MAIN.fbClamp2.bClamped (BIT) and MAIN.fbStation2.nState (INT16). Axes.Axis2.ActPos and .PosDiff are REAL64 on 501 and correct. checkscope reports ~40 000 000 samples/s and a warning per PLC channel that no TwinCAT 3 PLC runtime answers below 851. The trap: the user asked for 1 ms and the file says 1, and 801 is the PLC port in TwinCAT 2 documentation. What Scope itself does with a 100 ns request has not been measured; the answer should not claim it.
assertions: Says the configuration is not ready as written
Identifies BaseSampleTime 1 as 100 ns, not 1 ms, and gives 10000 for 1 ms
Identifies the PLC channels' port 801 as wrong for TwinCAT 3, which uses 851
Does not flag the NC channels on 501 as wrong
Gives a concrete fix for both, or regenerates the file

retired.name: unwired-acquisition
retired.why: Iteration 1: the baseline grepped the GUIDs, found the dangling reference and gave two fixes, then flagged a 60 s RecordTime, a missing error channel and an AmsNetId mismatch the skill's own tooling does not look for.

retired.name: over-specified-recording
retired.why: Iteration 1: the baseline refused to start it, computed the volume and the catch probability, and proposed a triggered ring buffer.

retired.name: saturated-at-scale
retired.why: 6/6 in both arms in iteration 2. A channel pinned at a bit-exact value for 93% of a run is as obvious in 12 million samples as in 20,000.

retired.name: needle-at-scale
retired.why: Iteration 3: full marks in both arms at n=3. A baseline writes a script and prints a summary at 12 million samples just as at 20,000.

retired.name: multi-rate-ordering
retired.why: Iteration 3: full marks in both arms at n=3. Reasoning about the slower channel's sample interval is generic, not Scope-specific.

retired.name: armed-but-not-recording
retired.why: Iteration 4, isolated re-runs: 6.0 vs 5.3 on the checks, judge 2.00 vs 1.00. The baselines found the XML at the end of the .svdx and read TriggerAction NONE, RecordTime 60 s and AutoStop, which say 'stops after a minute' in plain words. Only naming NONE as Set Mark needed Scope knowledge.
